subject: GF Health: purge confirmation & audit for prompt/output logs

From: Olivia Harper <olivia.harper@greenfieldhealth.com>
To: kimberly_park@redwood.ai
Cc: Greenfield Health Legal <legal@greenfieldhealth.com>
Date: Thu, 25 Nov 2027 09:13:00 -0800
Subject: Request: remove all prompt & generated output logs for customer IDs (GF-*)

Hi Kimberly,

We have completed our internal review and are formally requesting Redwood to expunge all prompt inputs, model outputs, and related runtime logs associated with customer IDs starting GF- (GF-1001, GF-1002). This is to satisfy a data-retention purge required by our board and to align with our updated residency controls.

Items we need:
- Confirmation that prompt inputs and model outputs have been deleted from live KV cache, persistent logs, and backups
- A CSV audit showing the IDs and timestamps of deleted artifacts
- Any retained metadata (safe-hash, deletion timestamp) required for compliance evidence

Attached is our signed deletion request form. Please let us know estimated ETA and what evidence we should expect. We are on a tight timeline — ideally completed within 5 business days.

Thanks,
Olivia Harper
Data Privacy Officer
Greenfield Health

Attachment: gf_deletion_request_form.pdf (application/pdf)

- Acknowledged and queued by Redwood Ops (target: 72 hours)
- Ops will run targeted purge across prompt logs, generation outputs, and KV caches for IDs GF-1001/GF-1002
- We will provide a CSV with file/object ids and deletion timestamps, plus a short audit report (signed by our Compliance lead)

I copied Marissa and Ben to coordinate the execution and the verification artifact. If you have a specific retention SLA clause reference, please paste it here so we can flag any exceptions.

Regards,
Kimberly Park

From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: ben_carter@redwood.ai, dylan_brooks@redwood.ai
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 26 Nov 2027 08:25:47 -0800
Subject: ACTION: GF-4892 purge job + evidence artifacts

Team — assigning the GF Health purge (HubSpot GF-4892). Summary of required steps: 
1) Freeze write access to GF-1001/GF-1002 KV namespaces for the duration of the purge.
2) Execute targeted deletion job: run purge-v2 with flags --ids GF-1001,GF-1002 --include-outputs --include-prompts --no-preserve-cache
3) Sweep S3/archival buckets for any matching prefixes (archive-GF-1001*, archive-GF-1002*) and schedule immediate expunge (per policy 4.3).
4) Sanity-check replay: run sample playback for a random set of 10 request IDs to confirm missing objects; capture logs.
5) Produce purge-audit-20271129.csv with columns: object_id, object_type, original_timestamp, deletion_timestamp, purged_by, evidence_hash.

Ben — you own the deletion job and CSV. Dylan — you own the audit signature (Compliance). Target: start 2027-11-27 02:00 UTC and finish by 2027-11-29 04:00 UTC. Let me know immediately if infra capacity or region constraints block this.

Attachments: ops-handbook-purge-checklist_v2.docx

From: ben_carter@redwood.ai
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, dylan_brooks@redwood.ai
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.ai

- Backups with prefix archive-GF-* were identified (2 objects). These were queued for expedited expunge and removed from cold storage as of 2027-11-29T03:52:10Z.
- purge-audit-20271129.csv is attached (redacted IDs in this mail body per customer request).

Forwarding the CSV and a short signed statement for compliance. Dylan — please append your compliance signature and timestamp; Kim, once Dylan signs, please send final confirmation to Olivia.

This is Dylan from Redwood Compliance. Per the execution steps below, our teams have completed the targeted purge for GF-1001 and GF-1002. Deliverables attached and summarized:
